fills.notes: The sequence in ¶1–4 is a list of pre-constructed containment-places (ditches, sea-place, plain, gehennas). The sea-giant likewise receives a prepared binding-place; the idiom expects a clause of confinement rather than a soteriological ‘fulfillment’.
The passage parallels ¶2’s ‘sea giant’: a second discharged power is the earth-bound counterpart whose fall prompts preparation of a place ‘below the four mountains’.
The sentence is stacking temporal clauses (‘Also, before…’) with a second ‘before’ introducing the next act in the chain of correspondential preparation.
The syntax requires a subject pronoun resuming the fallen entity: ‘the earth … fell to the sea and its thought shaped it’.

A prepared ‘place for it’ is specified as beneath cosmic supports (‘below the four mountains’). ‘Deep places’ preserves the impersonal cosmographic register of the substrate (a mapped region, not a named hell).
The line contrasts levels: below the four mountains / above the mountains of the heavens / above … . The missing term is the upper region being referenced.
The clause ‘that … a great plain it digs in Matter’ needs a verbal hinge expressing resultant formation: the prepared region turns into a plain carved in Matter.
After being smitten and thrown between mountains, something ‘is set fast upon it till the end’. In the substrate’s mechanics this is the restraining bond/fastening, not a moral sentence.
Parallel to later ‘they are thrown into the depths’: rebels and tyrants are first ‘cast outside’ (excluded from ordered regions) before being assigned hostels in the outer sea.
The whole chapter repeats the refrain ‘till the dissolution/end of the universe’. The hostels function as holding-stations ‘until the end’.
The abortions, like other swept-down residues, ‘fell down to the earth’; the gap likely contained the descent-verb plus particle.
Follows immediately: ‘they are gathered in and dwell therein’. So the prepared region is defined by its function (collection/containment) in correspondential, impersonal terms.

assessment: Most gaps can be constrained by the chapter’s repeated cosmographic pattern: before each class of discharge/rebellion/birth, a corresponding containment-region is prepared (inner sea-place, deep plain between mountains, gehennas, outer-sea hostels, gathering-place, prison, cities). Exact phrasing is firm where the surrounding syntax demands a specific verb or refrain (‘to tyrannise’, ‘until the end’), but several restorations remain tentative where the Coptic underlying formula could vary without changing the correspondential function (e.g., the precise hinge-verb around the ‘great plain’).
